units.cando: Can say what they and other people look like and what they wear, using I've got, his and her.
grammar: I've got … / He's got … / She's got …
his / her: His hair is short. Her eyes are brown.
lessons: My Face
say what your face looks like
I've got brown eyes. / I've got black hair.
My Body
say how many parts of your body you have got
I've got two hands. / I've got ten fingers.
My Clothes
say what clothes you have got and their colours
I've got a blue T-shirt. / I've got black shoes.
My Family Photo
describe people in your family with his and her
His hair is short. / Her eyes are brown. / He's got … / She's got …
New Clothes for Eid
say what new clothes people have got for Eid
He's got a new thobe. / She's got a new dress. / His shoes are black.
Who Is It?
describe a person and play a guessing game
He's got … / She's got … / His … is … / Her … are … / Is it …?

units.fnAr: التعبير عمّا أحب وما لا أحب
units.cando: Can say what food they like and don't like, and ask 'Do you like …?' and answer.
grammar: I like … / I don't like … / I love …
Do you like …? Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
plural food words: apples, bananas, eggs
lessons: Fruit I Like
say what fruit you like and don't like
I like … / I don't like …
Breakfast Time
ask and answer about breakfast food with 'Do you like …?'
Do you like …? Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
Lunch with the Family
talk about lunch food you like and don't like
Do you like …? No, I don't. I like …
Snacks and Sweets
say what snacks and sweets you love, like and don't like
I love … / I like … / I don't like …
A Picnic in the Desert
offer food and ask what people like at a picnic
Do you like …? Yes, I do. Here you are.
My Party Menu
plan a party menu by asking what people like
Do you like …? / I like … / I don't like … / Let's have …

units.cando: Can say what animals and people can and can't do, and ask 'Can it …?' and answer.
grammar: can / can't + verb: A fish can swim. A cat can't fly.
Can it …? Yes, it can. / No, it can't.
Can you …? Yes, I can. / No, I can't.
lessons: My Pet
say what pets can and can't do
A cat can run. / It can't fly.
On the Farm
ask and say what farm animals can do
Can it …? Yes, it can. / No, it can't.
At the Zoo
say what zoo animals can and can't do
It can climb trees. / Can an elephant jump? No, it can't.
In the Sea
ask and answer about what sea animals and you can do
Can dolphins swim fast? Yes, they can. / Can you swim? Yes, I can.
Move Like an Animal
say what you can and can't do like animals
I can jump like a frog. / I can't fly like a bird.
Guess My Animal
describe an animal with 'can' and 'can't' and play a guessing game
It's got … / It can … / It can't … / Can it …? / Is it a …?

units.cando: Can ask and say where things are in a bedroom, a school bag, a classroom and a living room.
grammar: Where is …? It's … / Where are …? They're …
Is it under …? Yes, it is. / No, it isn't.
lessons: My Bedroom
say where things are in your bedroom
It's in / on / under the …
My School Bag
ask and say where your school things are
Where's my pencil? It's in my pencil case.
In the Classroom
say where things are in your classroom with 'next to'
It's next to the window. / My desk is next to …
Toys in the Living Room
ask and say where many things are with 'Where are …?' and 'They're …'
Where are my cars? They're under the sofa.
Tidy Up!
say where things are and where they go when you tidy up
Where are …? They're … / Put them in / on the …
Treasure Hunt
play a treasure hunt by asking and saying where things are
Where's the treasure? / Is it under …? Yes, it is. / No, it isn't. / Here it is!

pages.text: Omar has a red magnet. It can pull things!
It picks up a spoon. It can't pick up a ball!
Grandpa is sad. "My key is in the grass. Where is it?"
"I can help, Grandpa!" Omar puts the magnet on a long stick.
Click! The key jumps to the magnet.
Grandpa smiles. "Thank you, Omar. You are a scientist!"

questions.q: What can the magnet pick up?

options: To find the key in the grass

"Grandpa, where is the baby camel?" "Oh no! I don't know!"
"Look, Grandpa! Little camel feet in the sand! Let's go!"
They walk to a big rock. "Listen! What's that?"
The baby camel is behind the rock! Noura gives it water.
They walk home together. Mama Camel is very happy!

questions.q: Why is Mama Camel very happy?

pages.text: Grandpa has got a big hat. The hat is on the table.
"Look! The hat is moving!" says Omar.
"Is it a monster?" asks Mona. "I don't know!" says Grandpa.
The hat jumps! Now it is on the floor.
Grandpa looks under the hat. A little kitten says, "Meow!"
Grandpa laughs. "Nice hat, kitten! It is your hat now!"

questions.q: Where is the hat at the start?
Who says the hat is moving?

pages.text: Omar and Grandpa are on a boat. The sea is big and blue.
"Look, Grandpa! A turtle!" "Oh no, Omar. It can't swim."
There is a bag on the turtle. Omar takes the bag.
The turtle swims away. "Bye, turtle!"
Then the turtle comes back. A baby turtle comes, too!
Omar puts the bag in the bin. "No bags in the sea!"

questions.q: Who comes back with the turtle?

pages.text: Oh no! Omar's red ball is in the tall tree.
Omar is small. The tree is very tall.
Omar has a long stick, a cup and some tape.
"Look, Mona! I can make a ball catcher!"
Up, up, up! Yes! The ball is in the cup!
Mona smiles. "Omar, you are an inventor!"

questions.q: Where is the ball at the start?
What does Omar use to make the ball catcher?
options: a stick, a cup and some tape

questions.q: Why can't Omar get the ball with his hands?
options: He is small and the tree is tall.

pages.text: We are at the airport. Look at the big plane!
I sit by the window. The clouds are white and soft.
Now we are in a new city. Where is my blue bag?
Oh no! There are ten blue bags!
Dad smiles. "Your bag has a yellow star, Omar."
I see it! This is my bag. Now let's go to Grandma's house!

questions.q: Where are Omar and Dad at the start?
How many blue bags are there?
How does Omar find his bag?

pages.text: This is Yusuf. He is small, but he can run fast.
The big boys play football in the park. "Can I play?" Yusuf asks.
"No, you are too small!" says Khalid. Yusuf is sad.
Oh no! The ball goes far, far away. The big boys are slow.
Yusuf runs fast. He kicks the ball. Goal!
"Wow! Please play with us, Yusuf!" says Khalid. Yusuf smiles.

questions.q: Where do the big boys play football?

options: The boys say he is too small.

questions.q: How does Khalid feel about Yusuf at the end?
options: He thinks Yusuf is a good player.
He wants Yusuf to go home.

stories.title: Big Bip and the Small Cat

pages.text: This is Bip. Bip is a big, blue robot.
Bip can carry a car! Bip is very strong.
Look! A small, white cat. Bip is scared!
Sara laughs. "Bip, it is only a cat!"
The cat jumps on Bip. "Meow!" says the cat.
Now the cat sleeps on Bip's head. Bip is happy!

questions.q: At the end, is the cat Bip's friend?
options: Yes, it sleeps on Bip's head.

pages.text: Sara and Grandpa walk in the desert. The sand is hot and yellow.
Sara sees something small. "Grandpa, look! What's this?"
"It's a coin," says Grandpa. "It's very, very old!"
They take the coin to the museum. A kind woman looks at it.
"Wow! This coin is from an old market," she says. "Thank you, Sara!"
Now the coin is in a glass box. A card says: "From Sara."

questions.q: Where do Sara and Grandpa walk?
What does "old" mean in the story?
Where is the coin at the end?
Why does the woman say "Thank you, Sara"?
options: Sara gives the coin to the museum

pages.text: "Look, Dad! A baby turtle on the beach!" says Sara.
The turtle is very small. It walks to the car lights, not to the sea.
"Oh no! The sea is here, little turtle!" says Omar.
Dad turns off the car lights. Now the turtle can see the moon on the sea.
The turtle walks and walks. Sara and Omar walk with it.
Splash! The turtle swims in the sea. "Goodbye, little friend!"

questions.q: Where does the turtle walk first?

options: He turns off the car lights

questions.q: Why does Dad turn off the lights?
options: So the turtle can find the sea

pages.text: It is Friday morning. Dad is sleeping.
Sara and Ali are in the kitchen. "Let's cook breakfast for Dad!"
Ali has three eggs. Oops! The eggs fall on the floor!
"Oh no! No eggs!" says Ali. "I know! Fruit salad!" says Sara.
Mum helps. They cut bananas, apples and oranges, and they put dates on top.
Dad comes to the kitchen. "Wow! It's yummy! Thank you!"

questions.q: Why do Sara and Ali make fruit salad?
How does Dad feel at the end?

pages.text: Sami wants a drum. But he has no drum.
Sami looks in the kitchen. He sees a big pot and two spoons.
Bang! Bang! "Sami, what is that?" says Mum.
"It is my drum!" says Sami. Mum smiles.
Baby Lina hits a cup. Ding! Grandpa claps his hands.
Now Sami has a band! They play and sing together.

questions.q: Where does Sami find the pot?
How does Mum feel at the end of the story?

stories.title: Detective Omar and the Red Ball

pages.text: I am Omar. I am a detective!
Oh no! Where is my red ball? It is not in my bag.
Look! Small feet on the floor. They are not my feet.
Listen! I can hear "Ha, ha!" under the table.
It is my baby sister, Lina! She has my red ball.
Lina is happy. We play with the ball. Good job, detective!

questions.q: Whose small feet are on the floor?

pages.text: Look! I have a red cape. I am Super Omar!
"Can you fly, Omar?" asks Mona. "No, but I can run fast!"
Oh no! A small cat is in the tree. It is sad.
Omar runs fast to Dad. "Dad, please help! A cat is in the tree!"
Dad is tall. He gets the cat, and Mona gives it milk.
"Thank you, Super Omar!" says Mona. "Your super power is your big heart!"
My family is camping in the desert. Our tent is big and green.
Dad makes a fire. We eat dates and look at the stars.
At night, I hear a sound. "What's that?" Sara asks.
Dad takes his lamp. "Let's look," he says.
It's a baby camel! Sara gives it a date.
Its mother comes, and they walk away. "Goodbye, little camel!" we say.

questions.q: What does Sara give the baby camel?
Why does the baby camel walk away?
options: It is scared of the fire
It wants to sleep in the tent

pages.text: "Look! A bird!" says Sami. It is in our classroom.
The bird is small and yellow. It is on the board.
"Sit down, please," says Mr. Ali. "Be quiet."
Sami opens the big window. The bird looks at the sky.
"Fly, little bird! Fly!" Now the bird is in the tree.
"Thank you, Sami!" says Mr. Ali. The bird sings, and we smile.

questions.q: Where is the bird in the classroom?
Why does Sami open the window?
options: He wants to see the tree

pages.text: This is my family. Today we go to the park!
Dad counts: "Mum, Sara, baby Ali, Grandma. Where is Omar?"
"Is Omar in the house?" asks Mum. "No!"
"Is Omar under the table?" asks Grandma. "No!"
"Look!" I say. "A big box in the car. It moves!"
"Hello! I am here!" says Omar. We all laugh. "Let's go!"

questions.q: Where does the family go today?

options: In a box in the car

questions.q: What does "under" mean in "under the table"?
How does the family feel at the end?

pages.text: This is Sara. She has a small robot. Its name is Beep.
Beep can walk and talk. "Hello, Sara!" says Beep.
Today Beep is very quiet. "Beep, are you sad?" asks Sara.
Sara looks at Beep. The little light is red!
Grandpa gives Sara a new battery. "Try this one!" he says.
The light is green! Beep dances. "Thank you, Sara and Grandpa!"

questions.q: What color is the little light first?
Who gives Sara a new battery?
"Beep is very quiet." What does "quiet" mean?

pages.text: This is Abbas. He loves the birds in the sky.
"I want to fly!" says Abbas. His friends laugh.
Abbas makes big wings. He puts on the wings.
He runs and jumps. Look! Abbas can fly!
Oh no! He falls down. He is not happy.
Abbas smiles. "Birds have tails. Now I know!"

questions.q: "His friends laugh." What do his friends do?
How does Abbas feel at the end?
options: happy, because he learns something new
sad, because he does not like birds

pages.text: It is very hot and sunny. Omar's little plant is dry and sad.
"Look, Grandpa! The sky is yellow!" "It is a big wind. Come inside, Omar!"
The wind is loud. Omar holds his cat, and they wait.
Now the sky is grey. Tap, tap, tap! "Grandpa, it is rain!"
Omar runs outside with his plant. "Drink, little plant, drink!"
The next day, the sun is back. "Look, Grandpa! My plant has a red flower!"

questions.q: What colour is the sky when the big wind comes?
Who does Omar hold when they wait inside?
Why does Omar take his plant outside?
options: To give it rain to drink
To show it to his cat
To put it in the wind

questions.q: How does Omar feel at the end of the story?

pages.text: Omar has a big paper. He wants to paint a tree.
He has red, blue and yellow paint. "Oh no! Where is the green?"
His sister Huda smiles. "Look, Omar!"
She puts blue and yellow together. Now it is green!
Omar paints a green tree. Then he puts red and yellow together. "Orange! For the sun!"
Mum puts the picture on the wall. "You are two great artists!"

questions.q: What does Omar want to paint?
Which color does Omar NOT have?
How does Mum feel about the picture?

pages.text: Sara finds Grandpa Ali's old watch. It is big and gold.
She turns it. Whoosh! The house is not here!
Sara sees sand, palm trees and a camel. A small boy has a red ball.
"Hello! I'm Ali. Can you play?" "Yes!" says Sara.
They play and laugh. Then Sara turns the watch again.
Grandpa has an old red ball. He smiles. "Thank you for playing, Sara!"

questions.q: What color is the boy's ball?
What does Sara see with the sand and palm trees?
Who is the small boy Ali?

pages.text: "Look, Dad! A big turtle on the beach!" says Omar.
Oh no! A plastic bag is on its head. The turtle is sad.
"Help it, Omar. Slowly!" says Dad. Omar takes the bag off.
The turtle is happy. It swims into the blue sea.
Omar looks at the sand. "Bottles, cans, bags! Come on, Dad and Sara!"
They put them in the bin. Now the beach is clean. "Goodbye, turtle!"

questions.q: What is on the turtle's head?
Why do Omar, Dad and Sara pick up the bottles and bags?
options: To keep the beach clean for animals
To give them to the turtle

pages.text: Yusuf is in the park. His big blue kite flies up, up, up!
A little girl, Noor, is crying. Her red kite is in a tall tree.
"Don't be sad," says Yusuf. "I can help you!"
Yusuf's dad is very tall. He gets the red kite down.
Oh no, it's broken! "Fly my kite with me," says Yusuf.
Noor smiles. Now two friends have one kite and two big smiles!

questions.q: Who gets the red kite down?
"Noor is crying." How does Noor feel?

options: He shares his kite with Noor.

pages.text: Omar and Dad walk on the beach. The sea is big and blue.
"Look, Dad! A small turtle is on the sand!"
The turtle is sad. It can't find the sea.
"A big bird is in the sky! Run, Omar!"
Omar holds the turtle. He runs to the water.
The turtle swims in the sea. "Bye, little turtle!" says Omar.

questions.q: Who walks on the beach with Omar?

options: The big bird can catch the turtle.

questions.q: How does Omar feel at the end?

pages.text: Sara is at Grandpa's farm. She can see a big camel.
"Grandpa, where is the baby goat?" "I don't know, Sara!"
Sara looks under the tree. She looks in the box. No goat!
"Listen!" says Grandpa. "Baa, baa!"
The baby goat is behind the camel! It is happy and warm.
Sara laughs. "Camel, you are a good friend!"

questions.q: What animal is Sara looking for?
Why does Sara say the camel is a good friend?
options: The camel keeps the baby goat safe and warm

pages.text: This is Sara. She has a red rocket.
"Look, Dad! My rocket can fly to the moon!"
Whoosh! The rocket goes up, up, up.
"Oh no! Where is my rocket now?"
Dad laughs. "Look, it is in our tree!"
Sara looks up at the moon. "One day, I can fly there!"

questions.q: Where is the rocket at the end?
What does Sara want to do one day?

pages.text: Omar has a new ball. It is red and white.
"Grandpa, can you play?" "Yes! I am the goalkeeper!"
Omar kicks the ball. Grandpa jumps and catches it!
"Again!" Omar kicks very hard. The ball goes up, up, up into the tree!
Grandpa shakes the tree. Down comes the ball, and three oranges!
The ball rolls into the goal. "Goal!" Omar shouts, and they eat the oranges.

questions.q: What colour is Omar's new ball?
Where does the ball go when Omar kicks very hard?
What does "shakes" mean in the story?
How does Omar feel at the end?

pages.text: Oh no! Mum's dates are not on the plate.
"Baba, is it you?" asks Omar. "Not me!" says Baba.
Omar looks at the floor. One, two, three small seeds!
The seeds go to the open window. Omar looks out.
A green bird is in the tree. It has a date!
Omar laughs. "Mum, the bird likes dates too!"

questions.q: What is not on the plate?
What does Omar see on the floor?

stories.title: The Red Kite in the Tree

pages.text: Omar has got a big red kite. It can fly high in the sky!
Oh no! The wind takes the kite into a tall tree.
"I can't get it," Omar says. He is very sad.
His friend Ali runs to him. "Don't be sad. I can help!"
Ali has got a long stick. Up, up... and the kite comes down!
"Thank you, Ali!" Now the two friends fly the kite together.

questions.q: What does "sad" mean in the story?
Why is Ali a good friend?
